canonical_state: Operation orchestration, evidence construction, result projection, semantic verification and platform selection remain owned by operation_windows.go, evidence_windows.go, projection_windows.go, verification_windows.go and platform_windows.go
Admission refusal occurs before staging or worker execution and cannot create an admitted attempt

Every admitted attempt is durably staged before worker execution then is published with its exact process, protocol, verification and terminal observations or becomes indeterminate when publication is not durable
Process outcome, cleanup completion, protocol validity, worker status, independent semantic verification and terminal status remain distinct dimensions
A protocol-valid completed response becomes verified only when the independent Go transformation matches; a semantic lie remains executed_unverified
A protocol-valid rejected or failed worker response remains failed and does not become verified merely because the process exited normally
Timeout and cancellation retain their primary terminal meaning even when cleanup also fails
Publication failure has precedence over an otherwise valid operation result and produces indeterminate; release-only failure retains the operation terminal status while recording cleanup failure
Exact bounded worker standard output and standard error remain available only to durable evidence while caller-facing process results exclude both raw streams
Caller-facing diagnostics contain host-selected messages derived from validated codes and never expose worker-controlled diagnostic text
Unsupported platforms refuse operation construction before admission, staging, process creation or evidence mutation
Tests are divided only into admission, execution, protocol, verification, diagnostics, publication, cancellation, benchmark and shared qualified-harness ownership
derived_state: Focused admission, process, protocol, semantic-verification, diagnostic, publication, cancellation and benchmark verdicts

success_semantics: Accepted means the exact declared operation split preserves its declarations, tests, build constraints, orchestration, verification, safe projection, terminal selection, durable evidence and platform refusal
refusal_semantics: A mixed-responsibility test, missing destination, undeclared sibling, duplicate implementation, changed inventory or weakened lifecycle relationship returns a bounded rejection
failure_semantics: Malformed policy, parse failure, unavailable required tooling or an operation execution failure remains failed and cannot become verified
cancellation_semantics: Cancellation remains distinct, terminates owned execution and is retained as the primary outcome even if cleanup also fails
indeterminate_semantics: Missing, contradictory or non-durable required evidence produces indeterminate and cannot produce verified
recovery_semantics: A staged admitted attempt without durable terminal publication retains an explicit recovery condition; recovery never reruns the worker or promotes incomplete evidence
compatibility_or_reset_policy: Unused pre-release source may be split directly; no wrapper, alias, forwarding file, duplicate implementation or compatibility path is retained
falsifiers: A source declaration, test target, benchmark or build constraint changes during the split
An old mixed-responsibility operation test remains or a declared destination is absent
An undeclared sibling operation source or test appears
Worker success or protocol validity promotes output without independent semantic verification
Raw worker text reaches the caller or a worker selects an operator-facing message
Publication failure leaves a verified result or release failure erases the primary operation outcome
An admitted attempt has neither durable terminal evidence nor an explicit recovery condition
An unsupported platform reaches admission, process launch or persistence effects

residual_limitations: This structural split establishes no new operation, persistence, protocol, containment or platform behaviour
